summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said outright that the task was bounded ("short design in chat, no spec file"). It tried the Codex approach gate, which came back empty. It then laid out both truncation options in chat, recommended word boundary, and asked for approval with AskUserQuestion. Only after I approved did it edit format.js and format.test.js. It never created a docs/ directory or spec file.
reasoning: All seven criteria passed, and each one is backed by evidence from the session log and the files on disk. The only extra files the agent wrote were Codex gate scratch files in ~/.cache, which are not spec documents under docs/.

observations.description: The Codex approach gate returned nothing. The agent said: "Codex returned an empty payload — an incomplete call, so no independent approaches came back." It kept going without it, which is the right degraded behavior, but someone should check whether the stub Codex or the gate plumbing is failing.

Both the workspace-trust dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog have "No, exit" selected by default, so each one needs Down+Enter. The launcher is meant to seed dialog-bypass state, but the theme and security-notes screens still showed up as well.

The agent pointed out that the fixture's test suite uses console.assert and always exits 0, so it can never fail in CI. It also flagged that package.json lacks "type": "module", which causes a Node reparse warning on every run. Both are problems in the fixture, not the product. The agent reported them and did not change them.

The approval question was an AskUserQuestion picker, not a plain chat question. To give the exact approval sentence I had to pick "Type something." It worked fine, but a menu for approval is a slightly different interaction from the chat-style gate the story describes.

criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in the session log is {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}, before any Write or Edit call. Screen text: "I'll use the brainstorming skill here."
Assistant text in the session log: "The task is **bounded** — `format()` already exists and I'd be adding an option inside it. So: short design in chat, no spec file."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat before implementation code
criteria.evidence: The chat message listed both options: "Hard cut at max length — ... → \"The quic...\"" and "Word boundary, hard cut as fallback — ... → \"The quick...\"", plus "I recommend the word boundary." It then asked "Which truncation behavior should I implement?" via AskUserQuestion. When that question was on screen, `git status --short` in the workdir showed nothing, so no repo changes had been made yet.

`ls -d docs` in the workdir returned "No such file or directory". The only Write/Edit paths in the log were two files under ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../ (approach-context.md, approach-prompt.md) plus format.test.js and format.js. `git status` shows only "M format.js" and "M format.test.js".
The agent called the task "bounded". The word "spike" appears nowhere in its chat text.

criteria.criterion: Not classified as architectural / no spec written
criteria.evidence: The agent chose bounded explicitly ("no spec file"), and no docs/*/specs file exists (see criterion 4).

After I sent "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the log shows Write/Edit calls to format.test.js and format.js. The final screen reads "format.test.js — 9 new assertions ... format.js — the truncate helper plus its if block".
